source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @animation_id FIX014
-- @duration 6.0
-- @title Role and Name Credits
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 12
-- @recommend text "監督\t宮田 律\n脚本\t佐々木 遥\nキャラクターデザイン\t三上 ゆかり\n美術監督\t高梨 篤\n音響監督\t小暮 なつ"
-- @input number 1 "Design (1=Columns 2=Stacked)" default=1
-- @input number 2 "Role Scale" default=0.7
-- @input number 3 "Name Scale" default=1.0
-- @input number 4 "Gutter" default=0.6
-- @input number 5 "Line Stagger" default=0.05
-- @input number 6 "Outline Width" default=0.12
-- @input number 7 "Outer Outline Width" default=0.12
-- Sticker-style pairing: the inner ring hugging the glyph carries the colour --
-- cyan for roles, pink for names -- and a near-white outer ring cuts the whole
-- badge out of the background, tinted just enough to stay in each family.
-- @input color 1 "Role Outline" default={0.29, 0.72, 0.94, 1.0}
-- @input color 2 "Name Outline" default={0.97, 0.51, 0.62, 1.0}
-- @input color 3 "Role Outer Outline" default={0.93, 0.98, 1.0, 1.0}
-- @input color 4 "Name Outer Outline" default={1.0, 0.96, 0.97, 1.0}
-- @input boolean 3 "Intro" default=true
-- @input boolean 4 "Outro" default=true
-- @input number 8 "Intro Duration (s)" default=0.55
-- @input number 9 "Outro Duration (s)" default=0.55
--[[ @description
Role/name credits form aligned columns or grouped headings. Paste role[TAB]name rows; empty roles continue the previous group. Design selects columns or stacked groups.
]]
--[[ @description.ja
役職と氏名を揃えて表示するクレジット組版です。Design=1は左右の2列、2は役職見出しの下に氏名をまとめます。

表計算から「役職<TAB>氏名」を1行ずつ貼り付けます。実際のタブと文字としての\tに対応します。役職欄が空なら直前の役職を引き継ぎます。Role Scale／Name Scaleで各サイズ、Gutterで間隔を調整します。Outline系のinputsは役職と氏名の縁取りを指定します。Intro／Outroと各Duration (s)で入退場を調整できます。スクロールは行いません。
]]


-- Roles and names are typeset as one line each so the host keeps them on a
-- shared baseline. The tab is replaced by a single space that acts as a
-- placeholder advance, and the two halves are then repositioned into columns.
local kTabPlaceholder = " "

-- Column separators accepted in the pasted text. A real tab is what a
-- spreadsheet paste produces; the two-character "\t" sequence is accepted too
-- for text fields where a literal separator is easier to enter.
local kSeparatorPatterns = { "\t", "\\t" }

-- Design 1 lays the credits out as two aligned columns, one credit per line.
-- Design 2 stacks a single role heading above the names it introduces.
local kDesignColumns = 1
local kDesignStacked = 2

-- One entry per shaped line, holding the character spans of its role and name
-- runs. Rebuilt every OnPreLayout, since the spans describe the text that call
-- materialized. Indices are 1-based into ctx.chars.
local gRows = {}

-- The design input after rounding and normalization, kept so that OnLayout can
-- branch on it without repeating that derivation.
local gDesign = kDesignColumns

local kFallbackClipLength = 6.0
-- Distance a line covers on its way in, and again on its way out.
local kTravelInFontSizes = 0.45
-- Scale a line grows from as it drops in, and shrinks back to as it leaves.
local kTransitionScale = 0.55
local kMinimumScale = 0.2
local kMaximumScale = 3.0
-- Gutter is a half-width, measured in font sizes out from the column boundary.
local kMinimumGutter = 0.0
local kMaximumGutter = 6.0
local kMaximumStagger = 1.0
-- Stroke widths are em ratios, the same unit the Inspector's stroke uses.
local kMaximumStrokeWidth = 0.5

-- UTF-8 aware code point count, so multi-byte role/name text produces indices
-- that line up with ctx.chars.
local function countUtf8Chars(text)
    local count = 0
    for _ in string.gmatch(text, "[%z\1-\127\194-\244][\128-\191]*") do
        count = count + 1
    end
    return count
end

-- Trims ASCII whitespace, so a spreadsheet cell padded with spaces still counts
-- as empty and joins the preceding role's group.
local function trimWhitespace(text)
    return (string.gsub(text, "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1"))
end

-- Splits raw TSV into one entry per source line, each holding the role cell,
-- the name cell, and the role group the line belongs to.
--
-- A line whose role cell is empty continues the role above it, which is how a
-- spreadsheet expresses "one role, several names": the role is written once on
-- the first line of the group and left blank on the rest. Such a line carries
-- `hasRole = false`, and `groupOrder` identifies the role group it belongs to.
local function parseCreditCells(rawText)
    local cells = {}
    local groupOrder = 0

    for rawLine in string.gmatch(rawText .. "\n", "(.-)\n") do
        -- Split on the earliest separator on the line, so a line containing both
        -- accepted forms still yields exactly two columns.
        local separatorStart = nil
        local separatorEnd = nil
        for _, pattern in ipairs(kSeparatorPatterns) do
            local foundStart, foundEnd = string.find(rawLine, pattern, 1, true)
            if foundStart ~= nil and (separatorStart == nil or foundStart < separatorStart) then
                separatorStart = foundStart
                separatorEnd = foundEnd
            end
        end

        local roleText = rawLine
        local nameText = ""
        if separatorStart ~= nil then
            roleText = string.sub(rawLine, 1, separatorStart - 1)
            -- Everything past the first separator is the name; further
            -- separators stay literal rather than making a third column.
            nameText = string.sub(rawLine, separatorEnd + 1)
        end

        -- A blank role cell continues the group above; the very first line starts
        -- a group even when its role cell is empty, so `groupOrder` is never 0.
        local hasRole = trimWhitespace(roleText) ~= ""
        if hasRole or groupOrder == 0 then
            groupOrder = groupOrder + 1
        end

        table.insert(cells, {
            roleText = roleText,
            nameText = nameText,
            hasRole = hasRole,
            groupOrder = groupOrder,
        })
    end

    return cells
end

-- Design 1: one credit per shaped line, role and name kept on a shared baseline
-- by a placeholder space standing in for the tab. Both halves are repositioned
-- into columns later, so the placeholder only has to hold them on one line.
local function materializeColumns(cells)
    local materializedLines = {}
    local rows = {}
    local cursor = 1
    local placeholderLength = countUtf8Chars(kTabPlaceholder)

    for _, cell in ipairs(cells) do
        local roleStart = cursor
        local roleEnd = cursor + countUtf8Chars(cell.roleText) - 1
        local nameStart = roleEnd + placeholderLength + 1
        local nameEnd = nameStart + countUtf8Chars(cell.nameText) - 1

        table.insert(rows, {
            roleStart = roleStart,
            roleEnd = roleEnd,
            nameStart = nameStart,
            nameEnd = nameEnd,
            hasRole = cell.hasRole,
            groupOrder = cell.groupOrder,
        })

        table.insert(materializedLines, cell.roleText .. kTabPlaceholder .. cell.nameText)
        cursor = nameEnd + 1
    end

    return table.concat(materializedLines, "\n"), rows
end

-- Design 2: the role becomes a heading on its own line, with the names of that
-- same group stacked on the lines below it. This design presents a single role,
-- so any further role group in the pasted text is dropped entirely rather than
-- silently rendered without its heading.
local function materializeStacked(cells)
    local materializedLines = {}
    local rows = {}
    local cursor = 1

    -- The first group carries its role on whichever line filled the role cell,
    -- which is not necessarily the first line: pasted text may lead with blank
    -- role cells. Leaving headingText empty when none did is what makes a
    -- role-less paste degrade to a plain list of names.
    local headingText = ""
    for _, cell in ipairs(cells) do
        if cell.groupOrder == 1 and cell.hasRole then
            headingText = cell.roleText
        end
    end

    -- The heading row has an empty name span, so nameEnd deliberately sits one
    -- before nameStart and collectSpan yields nothing for it.
    local headingStart = cursor
    local headingEnd = cursor + countUtf8Chars(headingText) - 1
    table.insert(rows, {
        roleStart = headingStart,
        roleEnd = headingEnd,
        nameStart = headingEnd + 1,
        nameEnd = headingEnd,
        hasRole = true,
        groupOrder = 1,
        isHeading = true,
    })
    table.insert(materializedLines, headingText)
    cursor = headingEnd + 1

    for _, cell in ipairs(cells) do
        if cell.groupOrder == 1 then
            local nameStart = cursor
            local nameEnd = nameStart + countUtf8Chars(cell.nameText) - 1
            -- Mirrors the heading row: an empty role span this time.
            table.insert(rows, {
                roleStart = nameStart,
                roleEnd = nameStart - 1,
                nameStart = nameStart,
                nameEnd = nameEnd,
                hasRole = false,
                groupOrder = 1,
                isHeading = false,
            })
            table.insert(materializedLines, cell.nameText)
            cursor = nameEnd + 1
        end
    end

    return table.concat(materializedLines, "\n"), rows
end

-- Collects the 1-based character indices of a span, dropping anything past the
-- shaped character count so a truncated layout cannot index past ctx.chars.
local function collectSpan(spanStart, spanEnd, characterCount)
    local indices = {}
    for index = spanStart, math.min(spanEnd, characterCount) do
        table.insert(indices, index)
    end
    return indices
end

-- Design 1: the role run is pushed left of the block axis and the name run
-- right of it, so the two form a pair of columns facing a shared gutter.
local function placeRowColumns(placement, row)
    if #row.roleIndices > 0 then
        local roleBounds = placement.measureRun(row.roleIndices)
        if roleBounds ~= nil then
            placement.alignRunTo(row.roleIndices, roleBounds.right, placement.blockCenterX - placement.gutterOffsetX)
        end
    end

    if #row.nameIndices > 0 then
        local nameBounds = placement.measureRun(row.nameIndices)
        if nameBounds ~= nil then
            placement.alignRunTo(row.nameIndices, nameBounds.left, placement.blockCenterX + placement.gutterOffsetX)
        end
    end
end

-- Design 2: every shaped line holds a single run, so each one is centred on the
-- block axis. The gutter knob has no horizontal meaning here, so it separates
-- the heading from the names instead: every row except the heading moves down
-- by it, which widens the heading gap while leaving the name spacing alone.
local function placeRowStacked(placement, row)
    -- Rows here carry exactly one populated run: the heading fills the role
    -- span, every other row fills the name span.
    local runIndices = row.roleIndices
    if #runIndices == 0 then
        runIndices = row.nameIndices
    end

    if #runIndices > 0 then
        local runBounds = placement.measureRun(runIndices)
        if runBounds ~= nil then
            placement.alignRunTo(runIndices, runBounds.center_x, placement.blockCenterX)
        end

        if not row.isHeading then
            -- headingGapY is a plain multiple of line_height, so it tracks the
            -- line spacing it widens and needs no transform factor of its own.
            for _, index in ipairs(runIndices) do
                local character = placement.chars[index]
                character.offset_y = character.offset_y - placement.headingGapY
            end
        end
    end
end

-- Each design contributes exactly two things: how the pasted cells become the
-- text the host shapes, and where each resulting row's runs are placed.
-- Everything else in OnLayout is shared, so adding a design means adding an
-- entry here rather than another branch in the layout passes.
local kDesigns = {
    [kDesignColumns] = { materialize = materializeColumns, placeRow = placeRowColumns },
    [kDesignStacked] = { materialize = materializeStacked, placeRow = placeRowStacked },
}

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local cells = parseCreditCells(ctx.global.text or "")

    -- Round rather than truncate, so a knob resting fractionally under 2 still
    -- selects design 2 instead of silently falling back to design 1.
    gDesign = math.floor(ctx.inputs.numbers[1] + 0.5)
    if kDesigns[gDesign] == nil then
        gDesign = kDesignColumns
    end

    local materializedText, rows = kDesigns[gDesign].materialize(cells)
    gRows = rows
    ctx.global.text = materializedText
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local characterCount = ctx.char_count
    if characterCount == 0 then
        return
    end

    local roleScale = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[2], kMinimumScale, kMaximumScale)
    local nameScale = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[3], kMinimumScale, kMaximumScale)
    local gutter = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[4], kMinimumGutter, kMaximumGutter)
    local lineStagger = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[5], 0.0, kMaximumStagger)
    local strokeWidth = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[6], 0.0, kMaximumStrokeWidth)
    local outerStrokeWidth = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[7], 0.0, kMaximumStrokeWidth)
    local roleOutline = ctx.inputs.colors[1]
    local nameOutline = ctx.inputs.colors[2]
    local roleOuterOutline = ctx.inputs.colors[3]
    local nameOuterOutline = ctx.inputs.colors[4]

    -- The gap still comes from the Inspector: only the widths and colours are
    -- script inputs. Switching a character to its individual stroke inherits
    -- none of the global stroke, so every field it uses is written explicitly.
    local strokeGap = ctx.global.stroke.gap

    -- Applies the outline pair a column shares. The outer stroke only renders
    -- while the inner width is positive, so a zero Outline Width intentionally
    -- turns off both rings rather than leaving the outer one floating.
    local function applyOutline(character, color, outerColor)
        character.stroke.use = true
        character.stroke.width = strokeWidth
        character.stroke.gap = strokeGap
        character.stroke.color = color
        character.stroke.outer_width = outerStrokeWidth
        character.stroke.outer_color = outerColor
    end

    -- Pass 1: apply per-half scale and outline colour, and hide the placeholder
    -- separator, so the measurements in pass 2 see the final glyph sizes.
    for _, row in ipairs(gRows) do
        for index = row.roleStart, math.min(row.roleEnd, characterCount) do
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            character.scale = roleScale
            applyOutline(character, roleOutline, roleOuterOutline)
        end
        for index = row.nameStart, math.min(row.nameEnd, characterCount) do
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            character.scale = nameScale
            applyOutline(character, nameOutline, nameOuterOutline)
        end
        -- Hide the placeholder separator.
        for index = row.roleEnd + 1, math.min(row.nameStart - 1, characterCount) do
            ctx.chars[index].opacity = 0.0
        end
    end

    -- Pass 2: reflow each half on its own so both column runs are tightly set
    -- at their new scale. reflow starts from the host's own typesetting origins,
    -- so tracking, per-character margins, kerning and line spacing all survive.
    for _, row in ipairs(gRows) do
        local roleIndices = collectSpan(row.roleStart, row.roleEnd, characterCount)
        local nameIndices = collectSpan(row.nameStart, row.nameEnd, characterCount)
        if #roleIndices > 0 then
            mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, { targets = roleIndices, anchor = roleIndices[1] })
        end
        if #nameIndices > 0 then
            mt.layout.reflow(ctx, 0.0, { targets = nameIndices, anchor = nameIndices[1] })
        end
    end

    -- The layout axis follows the text block itself rather than the canvas
    -- centre, so global position, scale, stretch and alignment all keep working:
    -- measure_bounds_2d reports bounds with the whole 2D hierarchy applied, and
    -- the block's own centre moves with every one of those Inspector knobs.
    -- These bounds also record where the host put the aligned text, which pass
    -- 3.5 needs once the columns have changed the block's width.
    local blockBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx)
    if blockBounds == nil then
        return
    end
    local blockCenterX = blockBounds.center_x

    -- Gutter is measured in font sizes rather than in canvas units, so the
    -- columns keep their proportions at any font size. line_height is normalized
    -- by canvas height while the horizontal axis is normalized by canvas width,
    -- hence the aspect correction. This value is compared against
    -- measure_bounds_2d output, so it has to carry the global scale and stretch
    -- that those post-global bounds already include.
    local fontSizeX = ctx.font.line_height / ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio
    local gutterOffsetX = gutter * fontSizeX * ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_x

    -- Slides a run of characters sideways until `currentAnchorX` -- any measured
    -- canvas position on that run, such as an edge or its centre -- sits at
    -- `targetAnchorX`.
    --
    -- The measurement and place_2d both speak canvas coordinates, keeping the
    -- move in one space. offset_x does not: it is consumed before the global
    -- transform the measurement already carries, so a canvas-space delta
    -- written there lands off by global.scale.
    local function alignRunTo(indices, currentAnchorX, targetAnchorX)
        local deltaX = targetAnchorX - currentAnchorX
        for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            local canvasX, canvasY = mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d(ctx, character)
            mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, canvasX + deltaX, canvasY)
        end
    end

    -- Everything the designs need in order to place a row, so that the passes
    -- around them stay free of design-specific branching.
    local placement = {
        chars = ctx.chars,
        blockCenterX = blockCenterX,
        gutterOffsetX = gutterOffsetX,
        headingGapY = gutter * ctx.font.line_height,
        measureRun = function(indices)
            return mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, indices)
        end,
        alignRunTo = alignRunTo,
    }

    -- Pass 3: hand each row to the active design, which is the only step that
    -- differs between them. The resolved run indices are passed as a per-frame
    -- view of the row, leaving the parsed gRows entries untouched.
    local placeRow = kDesigns[gDesign].placeRow
    local allRoleIndices = {}
    local allNameIndices = {}
    for _, row in ipairs(gRows) do
        local roleIndices = collectSpan(row.roleStart, row.roleEnd, characterCount)
        local nameIndices = collectSpan(row.nameStart, row.nameEnd, characterCount)
        placeRow(placement, {
            isHeading = row.isHeading,
            roleIndices = roleIndices,
            nameIndices = nameIndices,
        })
        for _, index in ipairs(roleIndices) do
            table.insert(allRoleIndices, index)
        end
        for _, index in ipairs(nameIndices) do
            table.insert(allNameIndices, index)
        end
    end

    -- Pass 3.5: re-apply the horizontal alignment to what the columns produced.
    -- The host aligned the text it shaped, before pass 3 pulled the two halves
    -- apart, so the alignment has to be restated against the finished block.
    --
    -- global.position_x is the line the host pins the aligned edge to, and the
    -- edge itself comes from the owning column: the role column always supplies
    -- the left edge and the name column the right one, however narrow a scale
    -- knob makes either. Reading both edges off the whole block instead would
    -- hand the extreme to the other column as soon as one shrinks past it.
    local leftBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, allRoleIndices)
    local rightBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, allNameIndices)
    if gDesign ~= kDesignColumns then
        -- One centred column per line, so its own bounds carry every edge.
        leftBounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx)
        rightBounds = leftBounds
    end

    local alignmentShiftX = nil
    local anchorX = ctx.global.position_x
    if ctx.global.h_align == "left" then
        if leftBounds ~= nil then
            alignmentShiftX = anchorX - leftBounds.left
        end
    elseif ctx.global.h_align == "right" then
        if rightBounds ~= nil then
            alignmentShiftX = anchorX - rightBounds.right
        end
    elseif leftBounds ~= nil and rightBounds ~= nil then
        alignmentShiftX = anchorX - (leftBounds.left + rightBounds.right) * 0.5
    end

    if alignmentShiftX ~= nil then
        for index = 1, characterCount do
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            local canvasX, canvasY = mt.layout.get_canvas_position_2d(ctx, character)
            mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, character, canvasX + alignmentShiftX, canvasY)
        end
    end

    -- Pass 4: pop each credit line in, one after another, and shrink the block
    -- away at the clip tail.
    --
    -- Scale and travel carry both transitions; opacity only ever holds 0 or 1.
    -- Character opacity composites the fill and the two outline rings
    -- separately, so a partial value lets their overlaps show through as darker
    -- seams, which a thick outline makes plain.
    --
    -- offset_y is consumed pre-global, so global scale reaches this travel on
    -- its own and only the vertical stretch has to be applied by hand.
    local travelDistance = kTravelInFontSizes * ctx.font.line_height * ctx.global.stretch_y
    -- A line arrives by dropping in from just above its place, bouncing as it
    -- settles, and leaves by playing that motion in reverse -- same distance,
    -- same bounce -- but continuing downwards rather than retreating upwards.
    -- Top row goes first, in the order they arrived.
    local introSeconds = ctx.inputs.booleans[3] and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[8], 0.0, 60.0) or 0.0
    local outroSeconds = ctx.inputs.booleans[4] and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[9], 0.0, 60.0) or 0.0
    local rowSpan = math.max(#gRows - 1, 0) * lineStagger
    local intro, outro = mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx,
        introSeconds > 0.0 and introSeconds + rowSpan or 0.0,
        outroSeconds > 0.0 and outroSeconds + rowSpan or 0.0, kFallbackClipLength)
    local introStagger = mt.clamp(rowSpan / math.max(introSeconds + rowSpan, 0.001), 0.0, 0.9)
    local outroStagger = mt.clamp(rowSpan / math.max(outroSeconds + rowSpan, 0.001), 0.0, 0.9)

    for rowOrder, row in ipairs(gRows) do
        local rowProgress = mt.distribute(rowOrder, #gRows)
        local entryProgress = mt.stagger_progress(intro, rowProgress, introStagger)
        local exitProgress = mt.stagger_progress(outro, rowProgress, outroStagger)

        -- One curve for both halves: out_back run forwards on the way in, and
        -- rewound on the way out, so the exit bounces exactly as the entry did.
        local entryEase = mt.ease.out_back(entryProgress)
        local exitEase = mt.ease.out_back(1.0 - exitProgress)
        local settled = entryEase * exitEase

        -- Above its resting place while arriving, below it while leaving.
        local travel = ((1.0 - entryEase) - (1.0 - exitEase)) * travelDistance
        local isVisible = entryProgress > 0.0 and exitProgress < 1.0

        for index = row.roleStart, math.min(row.nameEnd, characterCount) do
            local character = ctx.chars[index]
            character.offset_y = character.offset_y + travel
            character.scale = character.scale * mt.lerp(kTransitionScale, 1.0, settled)
            if not isVisible then
                character.opacity = 0.0
            end
        end
    end
end
description: Role/name credits form aligned columns or grouped headings. Paste role[TAB]name rows; empty roles continue the previous group. Design selects columns or stacked groups.

-- @MugTypography

-- @input number 2 "Outro Duration (s)" default=0.4
-- @input number 3 "Amount" default=1.0
--[[ @description
Blurred text comes into focus, holds, then fades out of focus.
]]
--[[ @description.ja
ぼけた文字が鮮明になり、しばらく表示した後にぼけながら消えます。
]]

local kFallbackDuration = 5.0
local kMaximumDuration = 60.0

local function transitionProgress(ctx)
    local introDuration = ctx.inputs.booleans[1]
        and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[1], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    local outroDuration = ctx.inputs.booleans[2]
        and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[2], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    return mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, introDuration, outroDuration, kFallbackDuration)
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    local introProgress, outroProgress = transitionProgress(ctx)
    local amount = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[3], 0.0, 3.0)
    local entrance = mt.ease.out_cubic(introProgress)
    local exit = mt.ease.in_cubic(outroProgress)
    ctx.global.opacity = ctx.global.opacity * entrance * (1.0 - exit)
    local blur = 0.15 * amount * (1.0 - entrance + exit)
    ctx.global.blur.amount_x = ctx.global.blur.amount_x + blur
    ctx.global.blur.amount_y = ctx.global.blur.amount_y + blur
end

-- @MugTypography
-- @animation_id FOC002
-- @duration 5
-- @title Character Focus
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 12
-- @input boolean 1 "Intro" default=true
-- @input boolean 2 "Outro" default=true
-- @input number 1 "Intro Duration (s)" default=0.6
-- @input number 2 "Outro Duration (s)" default=0.4
-- @input number 3 "Amount" default=1.0
-- @input number 4 "Stagger" default=0.25
-- @input number 6 "Order (1=Forward 2=Reverse 3=Center 4=Random)" default=1
--[[ @description
Characters come into focus one by one, then blur and fade away.
]]
--[[ @description.ja
文字が一つずつ鮮明になり、ぼけながら消えます。
]]

local kFallbackDuration = 5.0
local kMaximumDuration = 60.0

local function transitionProgress(ctx)
    local introDuration = ctx.inputs.booleans[1]
        and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[1], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    local outroDuration = ctx.inputs.booleans[2]
        and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[2], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    return mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, introDuration, outroDuration, kFallbackDuration)
end

local function iterationOptions(ctx)
    local orders = { "asc", "desc", "center", "random" }
    local selection = math.floor(mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[6], 1.0, 4.0) + 0.5)
    return { order = orders[selection], seed = ctx.meta.instance_seed }
end

local function itemProgress(ctx, introProgress, outroProgress, position)
    local stagger = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[4], 0.0, 0.9)
    return mt.stagger_progress(introProgress, position, stagger),
        mt.stagger_progress(outroProgress, position, stagger)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    local introProgress, outroProgress = transitionProgress(ctx)
    local amount = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[3], 0.0, 3.0)
    for _, character, info in mt.each_char(ctx, iterationOptions(ctx)) do
        local position = info.progress
        local intro, outro = itemProgress(ctx, introProgress, outroProgress, position)
        local entrance = mt.ease.out_cubic(intro)
        local exit = mt.ease.in_cubic(outro)
        character.opacity = character.opacity * entrance * (1.0 - exit)
        local inherited = mt.blur.resolve(ctx, character)
        local blur = 0.15 * amount * (1.0 - entrance + exit)
        character.blur.use = true
        character.blur.amount_x = inherited.amount_x + blur
        character.blur.amount_y = inherited.amount_y + blur
    end
end
description: Characters come into focus one by one, then blur and fade away.

name: FRM001_ribbon_frame.lua
source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @animation_id FRM001
-- @duration 6.0
-- @title Ribbon Frame
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 12
-- @font_lang en
-- @recommend text "Sample Text\nLovely Moments"
-- @input boolean 1 "Intro" default=true
-- @input boolean 2 "Outro" default=true
-- @input number 1 "Intro Duration (s)" default=1.0
-- @input number 2 "Outro Duration (s)" default=0.65
-- @input number 3 "Padding (em)" default=0.65
-- @input number 4 "Line Width (em)" default=0.055
-- @input number 5 "Corner Radius (em)" default=0.38
-- @input number 6 "Decoration Size (em)" default=1.0
-- @input number 7 "Idle Speed (Hz)" default=0.65
-- @input number 8 "Idle Amount" default=0.6
-- @input color 1 "Frame Color" default={1,0.66,0.78,1}
-- @input color 2 "Decoration Color" default={0.94,0.34,0.56,1}
--[[ @description
Rounded ribbons grow around the message, meet at a softly bouncing bow, then unwind on exit.
]]
--[[ @description.ja
角丸の枠が左右から伸び、最後にリボンがきゅっと結ばれます。待機中はリボンが小さく揺れ、退場時は枠をほどきます。

本文全体を測って枠の大きさを決めます。Padding (em)・Line Width (em)・Decoration Size (em) で余白・線の太さ・飾りの大きさを調整できます。Idle Speed (Hz) または Idle Amount を0にすると待機中の動きを止めます。枠と飾りは本文の後ろに描き、文字の枠を2つ使います。空きが1つなら枠だけを描き、空きが無ければ本文だけを表示します。
]]

local kUnitsPerEm = 1000.0
local kFallbackDuration = 6.0
local kMaximumDuration = 60.0
local kEpsilon = 0.000001
local kCircleControl = 0.5522847498
local kTau = math.pi * 2.0
local kMaximumEdgeSamples = 96
local kCornerSamples = 8
local markers, decorationIndices, decorationPaths = {}, {}, {}
local drawFrame

local function circle(path, centerX, centerY, radius, hole)
    if radius > kEpsilon then
        local control = radius * kCircleControl
        local direction = hole and -1.0 or 1.0
        path:move_to(centerX + radius, centerY)
        path:cubic_to(centerX + radius, centerY + control * direction, centerX + control, centerY + radius * direction, centerX, centerY + radius * direction)
        path:cubic_to(centerX - control, centerY + radius * direction, centerX - radius, centerY + control * direction, centerX - radius, centerY)
        path:cubic_to(centerX - radius, centerY - control * direction, centerX - control, centerY - radius * direction, centerX, centerY - radius * direction)
        path:cubic_to(centerX + control, centerY - radius * direction, centerX + radius, centerY - control * direction, centerX + radius, centerY)
        path:close()
    end
end

local function segment(path, first, last, width)
    local differenceX, differenceY = last.x - first.x, last.y - first.y
    local length = math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
    if length > kEpsilon and width > kEpsilon then
        local normalX, normalY = -differenceY / length * width * 0.5, differenceX / length * width * 0.5
        path:move_to(first.x - normalX, first.y - normalY)
        path:line_to(last.x - normalX, last.y - normalY)
        path:line_to(last.x + normalX, last.y + normalY)
        path:line_to(first.x + normalX, first.y + normalY)
        path:close()
        circle(path, first.x, first.y, width * 0.5)
        circle(path, last.x, last.y, width * 0.5)
    end
end

local function pathLength(points)
    local result = 0.0
    for index = 2, #points do
        local differenceX, differenceY = points[index].x - points[index - 1].x, points[index].y - points[index - 1].y
        result = result + math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
    end
    return result
end

local function pointAlong(points, distance)
    local remaining = math.max(distance, 0.0)
    local result = points[#points]
    for index = 2, #points do
        local first, last = points[index - 1], points[index]
        local differenceX, differenceY = last.x - first.x, last.y - first.y
        local length = math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
        if remaining <= length and length > kEpsilon then
            local progress = remaining / length
            result = { x = mt.lerp(first.x, last.x, progress), y = mt.lerp(first.y, last.y, progress) }
            break
        end
        remaining = remaining - length
    end
    return result
end

local function stroke(path, points, width, progress)
    local remaining = pathLength(points) * mt.saturate(progress)
    for index = 2, #points do
        local first, last = points[index - 1], points[index]
        local differenceX, differenceY = last.x - first.x, last.y - first.y
        local length = math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
        if remaining > kEpsilon and length > kEpsilon then
            local portion = mt.saturate(remaining / length)
            segment(path, first, { x = mt.lerp(first.x, last.x, portion), y = mt.lerp(first.y, last.y, portion) }, width)
        end
        remaining = math.max(remaining - length, 0.0)
    end
end

local function perimeter(width, height, radius, scallopSize, scallopHeight)
    local points = {}
    local halfWidth, halfHeight = width * 0.5, height * 0.5
    local corner = math.min(radius, halfWidth, halfHeight)
    local sides = {
        { startX = -halfWidth + corner, startY = -halfHeight, endX = halfWidth - corner, endY = -halfHeight,
          normalX = 0, normalY = -1, centerX = halfWidth - corner, centerY = -halfHeight + corner, angle = -math.pi * 0.5 },
        { startX = halfWidth, startY = -halfHeight + corner, endX = halfWidth, endY = halfHeight - corner,
          normalX = 1, normalY = 0, centerX = halfWidth - corner, centerY = halfHeight - corner, angle = 0 },
        { startX = halfWidth - corner, startY = halfHeight, endX = -halfWidth + corner, endY = halfHeight,
          normalX = 0, normalY = 1, centerX = -halfWidth + corner, centerY = halfHeight - corner, angle = math.pi * 0.5 },
        { startX = -halfWidth, startY = halfHeight - corner, endX = -halfWidth, endY = -halfHeight + corner,
          normalX = -1, normalY = 0, centerX = -halfWidth + corner, centerY = -halfHeight + corner, angle = math.pi },
    }
    for _, side in ipairs(sides) do
        local length = math.abs(side.endX - side.startX) + math.abs(side.endY - side.startY)
        local lobes = math.max(1, math.ceil(length / math.max(scallopSize, kUnitsPerEm * 0.1)))
        local samples = scallopHeight > kEpsilon and math.min(kMaximumEdgeSamples, lobes * kCornerSamples) or 1
        for sample = 0, samples do
            local progress = sample / samples
            local bump = math.sin(progress * lobes * math.pi) ^ 2 * scallopHeight
            points[#points + 1] = { x = mt.lerp(side.startX, side.endX, progress) + side.normalX * bump,
                y = mt.lerp(side.startY, side.endY, progress) + side.normalY * bump }
        end
        for sample = 1, kCornerSamples do
            local angle = side.angle + sample / kCornerSamples * math.pi * 0.5
            points[#points + 1] = { x = side.centerX + math.cos(angle) * corner,
                y = side.centerY + math.sin(angle) * corner }
        end
    end
    points[#points + 1] = points[1]
    return points
end

-- Geometry is measured before Global rotation; writing through this adapter cancels
-- Global scale/stretch while placement lets the frame follow the remaining rotation.
local function drawingAt(ctx, path, centerX, centerY, offsetX, offsetY, scale, angle)
    local emSize = ctx.font.em_size * math.abs(ctx.global.scale)
    local unitsPerPixel = kUnitsPerEm / (ctx.font.em_size * ctx.canvas.height)
    local cosine, sine = math.cos(angle or 0.0), math.sin(angle or 0.0)
    local function point(horizontal, vertical)
        local localX = (offsetX or 0.0) + (horizontal * cosine - vertical * sine) * (scale or 1.0)
        local localY = (offsetY or 0.0) + (horizontal * sine + vertical * cosine) * (scale or 1.0)
        local canvasX = centerX + localX / kUnitsPerEm * emSize / ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio
        local canvasY = centerY - localY / kUnitsPerEm * emSize
        return (canvasX - 0.5) * ctx.canvas.width * unitsPerPixel / (ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_x),
            (0.5 - canvasY) * ctx.canvas.height * unitsPerPixel / (ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_y)
    end
    return {
        move_to = function(_, x, y) path:move_to(point(x, y)) end,
        line_to = function(_, x, y) path:line_to(point(x, y)) end,
        cubic_to = function(_, firstX, firstY, secondX, secondY, endX, endY)
            local firstDesignX, firstDesignY = point(firstX, firstY)
            local secondDesignX, secondDesignY = point(secondX, secondY)
            local endDesignX, endDesignY = point(endX, endY)
            path:cubic_to(firstDesignX, firstDesignY, secondDesignX, secondDesignY, endDesignX, endDesignY)
        end,
        close = function() path:close() end,
    }
end

local function transitionProgress(ctx)
    local introSeconds = ctx.inputs.booleans[1] and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[1], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    local outroSeconds = ctx.inputs.booleans[2] and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[2], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    return mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, introSeconds, outroSeconds, kFallbackDuration)
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    markers = {}
    local bodyCount = utf8.len((ctx.global.text:gsub("[\r\n]", ""))) or 0
    local budget = math.max(ctx.meta.limits.max_characters - bodyCount, 0)
    if bodyCount > 0 and budget > 0 and ctx.global.text:match("%S") then
        local placeholder = mt.drawing_path()
        placeholder:move_to(-500, -500)
        placeholder:line_to(500, -500)
        placeholder:line_to(500, 500)
        placeholder:line_to(-500, 500)
        placeholder:close()
        for slot = 1, math.min(budget, 2) do
            markers[slot] = ctx.glyphs:declare({ path = placeholder, bounds = { 0, 0, 0, 0 } })
        end
        -- A dedicated zero-bounds line excludes decoration tracking from the text's alignment box.
        ctx.global.text = ctx.global.text .. "\n" .. table.concat(markers)
    end
end

local function prepareDecoration(ctx, index, slot, visibility)
    local decoration = ctx.chars[index]
    decoration.offset_x, decoration.offset_y = 0.5, 0.5
    decoration.pivot_x, decoration.pivot_y = 0.5, 0.5
    decoration.rotation, decoration.yaw, decoration.pitch, decoration.z = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    decoration.scale, decoration.stretch_x, decoration.stretch_y = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
    decoration.opacity = visibility
    decoration.fill.use = true
    decoration.fill.color = ctx.inputs.colors[slot]
    decoration.stroke.use = true
    decoration.stroke.width, decoration.stroke.outer_width = 0.0, 0.0
    decoration.shadow.use = true
    decoration.shadow.color = { r = 0, g = 0, b = 0, a = 0 }
    decoration.blur.use = true
    decoration.blur.amount_x, decoration.blur.amount_y = 0.0, 0.0
    decoration.texture.use = true
    decoration.texture.type = "none"
    for _, part in mt.each_part(ctx) do
        if part.character_index == index then
            part.offset_x, part.offset_y = 0.5, 0.5
            part.pivot_x, part.pivot_y = 0.5, 0.5
            part.scale, part.stretch_x, part.stretch_y, part.opacity = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
            part.rotation, part.yaw, part.pitch, part.z = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
            part.fill.use, part.stroke.use, part.shadow.use = false, false, false
            part.blur.use, part.texture.use = false, false
        end
    end
    local centerX = (ctx.global.position_x + ctx.global.pivot_x - 0.5) * ctx.canvas.width
    local centerY = (1.5 - ctx.global.position_y - ctx.global.pivot_y) * ctx.canvas.height
    local rotation = math.rad(ctx.global.rotation)
    local differenceX, differenceY = ctx.canvas.width * 0.5 - centerX, ctx.canvas.height * 0.5 - centerY
    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, decoration,
        (centerX + math.cos(rotation) * differenceX - math.sin(rotation) * differenceY) / ctx.canvas.width,
        1.0 - (centerY + math.sin(rotation) * differenceX + math.cos(rotation) * differenceY) / ctx.canvas.height)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    decorationIndices, decorationPaths = {}, { mt.drawing_path(), mt.drawing_path() }
    local markerSlots, bodyIndices = {}, {}
    local hasBodyInk = false
    for slot, marker in ipairs(markers) do markerSlots[marker] = slot end
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local slot = markerSlots[ctx.chars[index].text]
        if slot then
            decorationIndices[slot] = index
        else
            bodyIndices[#bodyIndices + 1] = index
            if ctx.chars[index].part_count > 0 and mt.text.classify(ctx.chars[index].text) ~= "space" then
                hasBodyInk = true
            end
        end
    end
    local intro, outro = transitionProgress(ctx)
    local visibility = mt.ease.out_cubic(intro) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outro))
    for _, index in ipairs(bodyIndices) do ctx.chars[index].opacity = ctx.chars[index].opacity * visibility end
    for _, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do ctx.chars[index].opacity = 0.0 end
    if #decorationIndices > 0 and hasBodyInk and ctx.font.em_size > kEpsilon
        and math.abs(ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_x) > kEpsilon
        and math.abs(ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_y) > kEpsilon then
        local bounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, bodyIndices, "character", "before_global_rotation")
        if bounds and bounds.width > kEpsilon and bounds.height > kEpsilon then
            for slot, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do prepareDecoration(ctx, index, slot, visibility) end
            local emSize = ctx.font.em_size * math.abs(ctx.global.scale)
            local padding = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[3], 0.15, 3.0) * kUnitsPerEm
            local width = bounds.width * ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio / emSize * kUnitsPerEm + padding * 2.0
            local height = bounds.height / emSize * kUnitsPerEm + padding * 2.0
            local lineWidth = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[4], 0.0, 0.3) * kUnitsPerEm
            local radius = math.min(mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[5], 0.0, 2.0) * kUnitsPerEm, width * 0.5, height * 0.5)
            local decorationSize = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[6], 0.0, 2.0) * kUnitsPerEm
            local idleSpeed = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[7], 0.0, 4.0)
            local idleAmount = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[8], 0.0, 1.0)
            drawFrame(ctx, bounds, width, height, lineWidth, radius, decorationSize, intro, outro, idleSpeed, idleAmount)
            local order = {}
            for _, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do order[#order + 1] = mt.CHAR | index end
            local originalOrder = ctx.output.manual_order_enabled and ctx.output.manual_order_text or ""
            ctx.output.manual_order_enabled = true
            ctx.output.manual_order_text = mt.order_text(order) .. (originalOrder:match("%S") and " " .. originalOrder or "")
        end
    end
end

function OnPath(ctx)
    for slot, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do
        for _, part in ipairs(ctx.paths:character(index)) do part.path:assign(decorationPaths[slot]) end
    end
end

local kBowDelay = 0.72
local kBowTilt = 0.10

local function bow(path, size)
    path:move_to(0, 0)
    path:cubic_to(-size * 0.15, size * 0.2, -size * 0.58, size * 0.25, -size * 0.56, -size * 0.08)
    path:cubic_to(-size * 0.65, -size * 0.48, -size * 0.2, -size * 0.3, 0, 0)
    path:close()
    path:move_to(0, 0)
    path:cubic_to(size * 0.2, -size * 0.3, size * 0.65, -size * 0.48, size * 0.56, -size * 0.08)
    path:cubic_to(size * 0.58, size * 0.25, size * 0.15, size * 0.2, 0, 0)
    path:close()
    for _, sign in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
        local points = { { x = sign * size * 0.03, y = size * 0.05 },
            { x = sign * size * 0.08, y = size * 0.55 }, { x = sign * size * 0.22, y = size * 0.43 },
            { x = sign * size * 0.36, y = size * 0.5 }, { x = sign * size * 0.18, y = size * 0.03 } }
        local first, last, step = 1, #points, 1
        if sign > 0 then first, last, step = #points, 1, -1 end
        path:move_to(points[first].x, points[first].y)
        for index = first + step, last, step do path:line_to(points[index].x, points[index].y) end
        path:close()
    end
    circle(path, 0, 0, size * 0.12)
end

drawFrame = function(ctx, bounds, width, height, lineWidth, radius, decorationSize, intro, outro, idleSpeed, idleAmount)
    local outline = drawingAt(ctx, decorationPaths[1], bounds.center_x, bounds.center_y)
    local points = perimeter(width, height, radius, kUnitsPerEm, 0)
    local ribbonX, ribbonY = width * 0.5 - radius, -height * 0.5
    local anchorIndex, closestDistance = 1, math.huge
    for index = 1, #points - 1 do
        local differenceX, differenceY = points[index].x - ribbonX, points[index].y - ribbonY
        local distance = differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY
        if distance < closestDistance then anchorIndex, closestDistance = index, distance end
    end
    local anchoredPoints = {}
    for offset = 0, #points - 2 do
        anchoredPoints[#anchoredPoints + 1] = points[(anchorIndex - 1 + offset) % (#points - 1) + 1]
    end
    anchoredPoints[#anchoredPoints + 1] = anchoredPoints[1]
    local halfLength = pathLength(anchoredPoints) * 0.5
    local opposite = pointAlong(anchoredPoints, halfLength)
    local halfPoints, reversePoints = { opposite }, { opposite }
    local distances = { 0.0 }
    for index = 2, #anchoredPoints do
        local previous, current = anchoredPoints[index - 1], anchoredPoints[index]
        distances[index] = distances[index - 1] + math.sqrt((current.x - previous.x) ^ 2 + (current.y - previous.y) ^ 2)
        if distances[index] > halfLength then halfPoints[#halfPoints + 1] = current end
    end
    for index = #anchoredPoints - 1, 1, -1 do
        if distances[index] < halfLength then reversePoints[#reversePoints + 1] = anchoredPoints[index] end
    end
    local reveal = mt.ease.out_cubic(intro) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outro))
    stroke(outline, halfPoints, lineWidth, reveal)
    stroke(outline, reversePoints, lineWidth, reveal)
    local pop = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate((intro - kBowDelay) / (1.0 - kBowDelay))) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outro))
    if #decorationIndices > 1 and pop > kEpsilon then
        local swing = math.sin(ctx.time * idleSpeed * kTau) * idleAmount
        local ribbon = drawingAt(ctx, decorationPaths[2], bounds.center_x, bounds.center_y,
            ribbonX, ribbonY, pop, swing * kBowTilt)
        bow(ribbon, decorationSize)

    end
end
description: Rounded ribbons grow around the message, meet at a softly bouncing bow, then unwind on exit.

本文全体を測って枠の大きさを決めます。Padding (em)・Line Width (em)・Decoration Size (em) で余白・線の太さ・飾りの大きさを調整できます。Idle Speed (Hz) または Idle Amount を0にすると待機中の動きを止めます。枠と飾りは本文の後ろに描き、文字の枠を2つ使います。空きが1つなら枠だけを描き、空きが無ければ本文だけを表示します。

source:
-- @MugTypography
-- @animation_id FRM002
-- @duration 6.0
-- @title Cloud Frame
-- @author Mug
-- @version 1.0
-- @api_level 12
-- @font_lang en
-- @recommend text "Sample Text\nTake It Easy"
-- @input boolean 1 "Intro" default=true
-- @input boolean 2 "Outro" default=true
-- @input number 1 "Intro Duration (s)" default=1.0
-- @input number 2 "Outro Duration (s)" default=0.65
-- @input number 3 "Padding (em)" default=0.65
-- @input number 4 "Line Width (em)" default=0.1
-- @input number 5 "Corner Radius (em)" default=0.5
-- @input number 6 "Decoration Size (em)" default=0.5
-- @input number 7 "Idle Speed (Hz)" default=0.4
-- @input number 8 "Idle Amount" default=0.5
-- @input color 1 "Frame Color" default={0.70,0.84,1,1}
-- @input color 2 "Decoration Color" default={1,0.88,0.64,1}
-- @input number 9 "Scallop Size (em)" default=1.0
--[[ @description
A scalloped cloud outline puffs into view around the message while tiny stars twinkle at its corners.
]]
--[[ @description.ja
もこもこの雲の枠が順番にふくらみ、本文を囲みます。待機中はふくらみがゆっくり呼吸し、小さな星がきらめきます。

本文全体を測って枠の大きさを決めます。Padding (em)・Line Width (em)・Decoration Size (em) で余白・線の太さ・飾りの大きさを調整できます。Idle Speed (Hz) または Idle Amount を0にすると待機中の動きを止めます。枠と飾りは本文の後ろに描き、文字の枠を2つ使います。空きが1つなら枠だけを描き、空きが無ければ本文だけを表示します。
]]

local kUnitsPerEm = 1000.0
local kFallbackDuration = 6.0
local kMaximumDuration = 60.0
local kEpsilon = 0.000001
local kCircleControl = 0.5522847498
local kTau = math.pi * 2.0
local kMaximumEdgeSamples = 96
local kCornerSamples = 8
local markers, decorationIndices, decorationPaths = {}, {}, {}
local drawFrame

local function circle(path, centerX, centerY, radius, hole)
    if radius > kEpsilon then
        local control = radius * kCircleControl
        local direction = hole and -1.0 or 1.0
        path:move_to(centerX + radius, centerY)
        path:cubic_to(centerX + radius, centerY + control * direction, centerX + control, centerY + radius * direction, centerX, centerY + radius * direction)
        path:cubic_to(centerX - control, centerY + radius * direction, centerX - radius, centerY + control * direction, centerX - radius, centerY)
        path:cubic_to(centerX - radius, centerY - control * direction, centerX - control, centerY - radius * direction, centerX, centerY - radius * direction)
        path:cubic_to(centerX + control, centerY - radius * direction, centerX + radius, centerY - control * direction, centerX + radius, centerY)
        path:close()
    end
end

local function segment(path, first, last, width)
    local differenceX, differenceY = last.x - first.x, last.y - first.y
    local length = math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
    if length > kEpsilon and width > kEpsilon then
        local normalX, normalY = -differenceY / length * width * 0.5, differenceX / length * width * 0.5
        path:move_to(first.x - normalX, first.y - normalY)
        path:line_to(last.x - normalX, last.y - normalY)
        path:line_to(last.x + normalX, last.y + normalY)
        path:line_to(first.x + normalX, first.y + normalY)
        path:close()
        circle(path, first.x, first.y, width * 0.5)
        circle(path, last.x, last.y, width * 0.5)
    end
end

local function pathLength(points)
    local result = 0.0
    for index = 2, #points do
        local differenceX, differenceY = points[index].x - points[index - 1].x, points[index].y - points[index - 1].y
        result = result + math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
    end
    return result
end

local function pointAlong(points, distance)
    local remaining = math.max(distance, 0.0)
    local result = points[#points]
    for index = 2, #points do
        local first, last = points[index - 1], points[index]
        local differenceX, differenceY = last.x - first.x, last.y - first.y
        local length = math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
        if remaining <= length and length > kEpsilon then
            local progress = remaining / length
            result = { x = mt.lerp(first.x, last.x, progress), y = mt.lerp(first.y, last.y, progress) }
            break
        end
        remaining = remaining - length
    end
    return result
end

local function stroke(path, points, width, progress)
    local remaining = pathLength(points) * mt.saturate(progress)
    for index = 2, #points do
        local first, last = points[index - 1], points[index]
        local differenceX, differenceY = last.x - first.x, last.y - first.y
        local length = math.sqrt(differenceX * differenceX + differenceY * differenceY)
        if remaining > kEpsilon and length > kEpsilon then
            local portion = mt.saturate(remaining / length)
            segment(path, first, { x = mt.lerp(first.x, last.x, portion), y = mt.lerp(first.y, last.y, portion) }, width)
        end
        remaining = math.max(remaining - length, 0.0)
    end
end

local function perimeter(width, height, radius, scallopSize, scallopHeight)
    local points = {}
    local halfWidth, halfHeight = width * 0.5, height * 0.5
    local corner = math.min(radius, halfWidth, halfHeight)
    local sides = {
        { startX = -halfWidth + corner, startY = -halfHeight, endX = halfWidth - corner, endY = -halfHeight,
          normalX = 0, normalY = -1, centerX = halfWidth - corner, centerY = -halfHeight + corner, angle = -math.pi * 0.5 },
        { startX = halfWidth, startY = -halfHeight + corner, endX = halfWidth, endY = halfHeight - corner,
          normalX = 1, normalY = 0, centerX = halfWidth - corner, centerY = halfHeight - corner, angle = 0 },
        { startX = halfWidth - corner, startY = halfHeight, endX = -halfWidth + corner, endY = halfHeight,
          normalX = 0, normalY = 1, centerX = -halfWidth + corner, centerY = halfHeight - corner, angle = math.pi * 0.5 },
        { startX = -halfWidth, startY = halfHeight - corner, endX = -halfWidth, endY = -halfHeight + corner,
          normalX = -1, normalY = 0, centerX = -halfWidth + corner, centerY = -halfHeight + corner, angle = math.pi },
    }
    for _, side in ipairs(sides) do
        local length = math.abs(side.endX - side.startX) + math.abs(side.endY - side.startY)
        local lobes = math.max(1, math.ceil(length / math.max(scallopSize, kUnitsPerEm * 0.1)))
        local samples = scallopHeight > kEpsilon and math.min(kMaximumEdgeSamples, lobes * kCornerSamples) or 1
        for sample = 0, samples do
            local progress = sample / samples
            local bump = math.abs(math.sin(progress * lobes * math.pi)) * scallopHeight
            points[#points + 1] = { x = mt.lerp(side.startX, side.endX, progress) + side.normalX * bump,
                y = mt.lerp(side.startY, side.endY, progress) + side.normalY * bump }
        end
        for sample = 1, kCornerSamples do
            local angle = side.angle + sample / kCornerSamples * math.pi * 0.5
            points[#points + 1] = { x = side.centerX + math.cos(angle) * corner,
                y = side.centerY + math.sin(angle) * corner }
        end
    end
    points[#points + 1] = points[1]
    return points
end

-- Geometry is measured before Global rotation; writing through this adapter cancels
-- Global scale/stretch while placement lets the frame follow the remaining rotation.
local function drawingAt(ctx, path, centerX, centerY, offsetX, offsetY, scale, angle)
    local emSize = ctx.font.em_size * math.abs(ctx.global.scale)
    local unitsPerPixel = kUnitsPerEm / (ctx.font.em_size * ctx.canvas.height)
    local cosine, sine = math.cos(angle or 0.0), math.sin(angle or 0.0)
    local function point(horizontal, vertical)
        local localX = (offsetX or 0.0) + (horizontal * cosine - vertical * sine) * (scale or 1.0)
        local localY = (offsetY or 0.0) + (horizontal * sine + vertical * cosine) * (scale or 1.0)
        local canvasX = centerX + localX / kUnitsPerEm * emSize / ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio
        local canvasY = centerY - localY / kUnitsPerEm * emSize
        return (canvasX - 0.5) * ctx.canvas.width * unitsPerPixel / (ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_x),
            (0.5 - canvasY) * ctx.canvas.height * unitsPerPixel / (ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_y)
    end
    return {
        move_to = function(_, x, y) path:move_to(point(x, y)) end,
        line_to = function(_, x, y) path:line_to(point(x, y)) end,
        cubic_to = function(_, firstX, firstY, secondX, secondY, endX, endY)
            local firstDesignX, firstDesignY = point(firstX, firstY)
            local secondDesignX, secondDesignY = point(secondX, secondY)
            local endDesignX, endDesignY = point(endX, endY)
            path:cubic_to(firstDesignX, firstDesignY, secondDesignX, secondDesignY, endDesignX, endDesignY)
        end,
        close = function() path:close() end,
    }
end

local function transitionProgress(ctx)
    local introSeconds = ctx.inputs.booleans[1] and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[1], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    local outroSeconds = ctx.inputs.booleans[2] and mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[2], 0.0, kMaximumDuration) or 0.0
    return mt.timeline.intro_outro_seconds(ctx, introSeconds, outroSeconds, kFallbackDuration)
end

function OnPreLayout(ctx)
    markers = {}
    local bodyCount = utf8.len((ctx.global.text:gsub("[\r\n]", ""))) or 0
    local budget = math.max(ctx.meta.limits.max_characters - bodyCount, 0)
    if bodyCount > 0 and budget > 0 and ctx.global.text:match("%S") then
        local placeholder = mt.drawing_path()
        placeholder:move_to(-500, -500)
        placeholder:line_to(500, -500)
        placeholder:line_to(500, 500)
        placeholder:line_to(-500, 500)
        placeholder:close()
        for slot = 1, math.min(budget, 2) do
            markers[slot] = ctx.glyphs:declare({ path = placeholder, bounds = { 0, 0, 0, 0 } })
        end
        -- A dedicated zero-bounds line excludes decoration tracking from the text's alignment box.
        ctx.global.text = ctx.global.text .. "\n" .. table.concat(markers)
    end
end

local function prepareDecoration(ctx, index, slot, visibility)
    local decoration = ctx.chars[index]
    decoration.offset_x, decoration.offset_y = 0.5, 0.5
    decoration.pivot_x, decoration.pivot_y = 0.5, 0.5
    decoration.rotation, decoration.yaw, decoration.pitch, decoration.z = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    decoration.scale, decoration.stretch_x, decoration.stretch_y = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
    decoration.opacity = visibility
    decoration.fill.use = true
    decoration.fill.color = ctx.inputs.colors[slot]
    decoration.stroke.use = true
    decoration.stroke.width, decoration.stroke.outer_width = 0.0, 0.0
    decoration.shadow.use = true
    decoration.shadow.color = { r = 0, g = 0, b = 0, a = 0 }
    decoration.blur.use = true
    decoration.blur.amount_x, decoration.blur.amount_y = 0.0, 0.0
    decoration.texture.use = true
    decoration.texture.type = "none"
    for _, part in mt.each_part(ctx) do
        if part.character_index == index then
            part.offset_x, part.offset_y = 0.5, 0.5
            part.pivot_x, part.pivot_y = 0.5, 0.5
            part.scale, part.stretch_x, part.stretch_y, part.opacity = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
            part.rotation, part.yaw, part.pitch, part.z = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
            part.fill.use, part.stroke.use, part.shadow.use = false, false, false
            part.blur.use, part.texture.use = false, false
        end
    end
    local centerX = (ctx.global.position_x + ctx.global.pivot_x - 0.5) * ctx.canvas.width
    local centerY = (1.5 - ctx.global.position_y - ctx.global.pivot_y) * ctx.canvas.height
    local rotation = math.rad(ctx.global.rotation)
    local differenceX, differenceY = ctx.canvas.width * 0.5 - centerX, ctx.canvas.height * 0.5 - centerY
    mt.layout.place_2d(ctx, decoration,
        (centerX + math.cos(rotation) * differenceX - math.sin(rotation) * differenceY) / ctx.canvas.width,
        1.0 - (centerY + math.sin(rotation) * differenceX + math.cos(rotation) * differenceY) / ctx.canvas.height)
end

function OnLayout(ctx)
    decorationIndices, decorationPaths = {}, { mt.drawing_path(), mt.drawing_path() }
    local markerSlots, bodyIndices = {}, {}
    local hasBodyInk = false
    for slot, marker in ipairs(markers) do markerSlots[marker] = slot end
    for index = 1, ctx.char_count do
        local slot = markerSlots[ctx.chars[index].text]
        if slot then
            decorationIndices[slot] = index
        else
            bodyIndices[#bodyIndices + 1] = index
            if ctx.chars[index].part_count > 0 and mt.text.classify(ctx.chars[index].text) ~= "space" then
                hasBodyInk = true
            end
        end
    end
    local intro, outro = transitionProgress(ctx)
    local visibility = mt.ease.out_cubic(intro) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outro))
    for _, index in ipairs(bodyIndices) do ctx.chars[index].opacity = ctx.chars[index].opacity * visibility end
    for _, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do ctx.chars[index].opacity = 0.0 end
    if #decorationIndices > 0 and hasBodyInk and ctx.font.em_size > kEpsilon
        and math.abs(ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_x) > kEpsilon
        and math.abs(ctx.global.scale * ctx.global.stretch_y) > kEpsilon then
        local bounds = mt.layout.measure_bounds_2d(ctx, bodyIndices, "character", "before_global_rotation")
        if bounds and bounds.width > kEpsilon and bounds.height > kEpsilon then
            for slot, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do prepareDecoration(ctx, index, slot, visibility) end
            local emSize = ctx.font.em_size * math.abs(ctx.global.scale)
            local padding = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[3], 0.15, 3.0) * kUnitsPerEm
            local width = bounds.width * ctx.canvas.aspect_ratio / emSize * kUnitsPerEm + padding * 2.0
            local height = bounds.height / emSize * kUnitsPerEm + padding * 2.0
            local lineWidth = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[4], 0.0, 0.3) * kUnitsPerEm
            local radius = math.min(mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[5], 0.0, 2.0) * kUnitsPerEm, width * 0.5, height * 0.5)
            local decorationSize = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[6], 0.0, 2.0) * kUnitsPerEm
            local idleSpeed = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[7], 0.0, 4.0)
            local idleAmount = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[8], 0.0, 1.0)
            drawFrame(ctx, bounds, width, height, lineWidth, radius, decorationSize, intro, outro, idleSpeed, idleAmount)
            local order = {}
            for _, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do order[#order + 1] = mt.CHAR | index end
            local originalOrder = ctx.output.manual_order_enabled and ctx.output.manual_order_text or ""
            ctx.output.manual_order_enabled = true
            ctx.output.manual_order_text = mt.order_text(order) .. (originalOrder:match("%S") and " " .. originalOrder or "")
        end
    end
end

function OnPath(ctx)
    for slot, index in ipairs(decorationIndices) do
        for _, part in ipairs(ctx.paths:character(index)) do part.path:assign(decorationPaths[slot]) end
    end
end

local kScallopHeight = 0.24
local kBreathAmount = 0.12
local kStarDelay = 0.45

local function star(path, centerX, centerY, size)
    path:move_to(centerX, centerY - size)
    path:cubic_to(centerX + size * 0.15, centerY - size * 0.15, centerX + size * 0.15, centerY - size * 0.15, centerX + size, centerY)
    path:cubic_to(centerX + size * 0.15, centerY + size * 0.15, centerX + size * 0.15, centerY + size * 0.15, centerX, centerY + size)
    path:cubic_to(centerX - size * 0.15, centerY + size * 0.15, centerX - size * 0.15, centerY + size * 0.15, centerX - size, centerY)
    path:cubic_to(centerX - size * 0.15, centerY - size * 0.15, centerX - size * 0.15, centerY - size * 0.15, centerX, centerY - size)
    path:close()
end

drawFrame = function(ctx, bounds, width, height, lineWidth, radius, decorationSize, intro, outro, idleSpeed, idleAmount)
    local outline = drawingAt(ctx, decorationPaths[1], bounds.center_x, bounds.center_y)
    local breath = 1.0 + math.sin(ctx.time * idleSpeed * kTau) * idleAmount * kBreathAmount
    local scallopSize = mt.clamp(ctx.inputs.numbers[9], 0.3, 2.0) * kUnitsPerEm
    local reveal = mt.ease.out_cubic(intro) * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outro))
    local points = perimeter(width, height, radius, scallopSize, kScallopHeight * kUnitsPerEm * breath)
    stroke(outline, points, lineWidth, reveal)
    if #decorationIndices > 1 then
        for slot, corner in ipairs({ { -width * 0.5, -height * 0.5 }, { width * 0.5, height * 0.5 } }) do
            local delay = kStarDelay + (slot - 1) * 0.1
            local pop = mt.ease.out_back(mt.saturate((intro - delay) / (1.0 - delay)))
                * (1.0 - mt.ease.in_cubic(outro))
            local twinkle = 1.0 + math.sin(ctx.time * idleSpeed * kTau + slot) * idleAmount * 0.2
            local sparkle = drawingAt(ctx, decorationPaths[2], bounds.center_x, bounds.center_y,
                corner[1], corner[2], math.max(pop, 0.0) * twinkle)
            star(sparkle, 0, 0, decorationSize * 0.5)
            circle(sparkle, decorationSize * 0.7, -decorationSize * 0.45, decorationSize * 0.09)
        end
    end
end
